```{r}
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "report_card.R"))

# Numbers for the stat boxes, from the same status file as the tiles
status_now <- read_status()
n_ind      <- nrow(status_now)
n_poor     <- sum(status_now$status == "poor")
n_good     <- sum(status_now$status == "good")

# Hero background: one stripe per year of sea temperature at Stonehaven,
# brighter in warmer years (annual anomalies from the Sea temperature page)
temp <- readr::read_csv(here::here("data", "processed", "sea_temp_annual.csv"),
                        show_col_types = FALSE)
st   <- temp[temp$site == "Stonehaven", ]
st   <- st[order(st$year), ]
stripe_col <- scales::col_numeric(c("#1d1f14", "#5f6b1e", "#a7b544", "#dbe58a"),
                                  domain = range(st$anom))(st$anom)
rects <- sprintf('<rect x="%d" y="0" width="1.02" height="1" fill="%s"></rect>',
                 seq_along(stripe_col) - 1, stripe_col)
stripes_html <- sprintf(
  '<div class="hero-bg" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 %d 1" preserveAspectRatio="none">%s</svg></div>',
  length(stripe_col), paste(rects, collapse = ""))
stripe_years <- paste(min(st$year), "to", max(st$year))
```


# State of Scotland's Seas. [Seabirds, seals, salmon, sea temperature, and protected areas.]{.accent}

An independent, reproducible indicator report card built from open data. Five indicators, one featured deep dive on seabirds after avian influenza, and a framework map linking each indicator to the targets and conventions it reports against.

[See the report card](#at-a-glance){.btn .btn-accent} [Seabirds deep dive](indicators/seabirds.qmd){.btn .btn-ghost} [Code on GitHub](https://github.com/emmabranch/scotland-seas-indicators){.btn .btn-ghost}

```{r}

cat(sprintf('<p class="hero-note">Background: one stripe per year of sea temperature at Stonehaven, %s, brighter in warmer years.</p>', stripe_years))
```

## At a glance

```{r}
report_card()
```

```{r}
status_legend()
```

Confidence (●●● high, ●●○ medium, ●○○ low) reflects how far the data can support the status call: coverage, survey frequency, and known gaps. Each tile links to the full indicator page, with methods and limitations.

## How to read this report card

- **Status** summarises recent condition in plain language. It is my independent judgement from the published data, not an official assessment.
- **Trend** describes direction of change over the period shown. Sea temperature is a context indicator, so it has no "good" or "bad" direction.
- **Confidence** is reported separately so a clear trend in patchy data is not mistaken for a certain one.
